finite_dimensional_interface.state: arbitrary tau_ABC, with no requirement dim(B)=dim(C) or marginal symmetry
finite_dimensional_interface.target: dimension-free trace-distance proximity to Sep(A:BC) as delta_B+delta_C tends to zero
finite_dimensional_interface.stronger_target: one B-local EB reconstruction of tau_AB plus a compatible recovery of tau_ABC

known_exact_endpoint: Hayashi-Zhao, arXiv:2601.09995v1, Theorem 1: exact A-B-C and A-C-B Markov conditions iff locally readable PVM labels on B and C induce a common classical J with I(A:BC|J)=0; hence tau_ABC is separable across A:BC.
closest_approximate_antecedent: Fawzi-Renner gives a separate recovery map for each one-sided small CMI, not a common label, EB map, or separable approximation.
one_sided_counterexample_status: Ibinson-Linden-Winter one-CMI Markov-distance examples do not establish failure of the two-CMI, bounded-I(A:B) separability target; checked symmetric-subspace example has opposite CMI and I(A:B) growing as log(d(d+1)/2).
fixed_dimension_status: Compactness plus the exact theorem yields a dimension-dependent qualitative modulus only for fixed local dimensions.
decisive_missing_lemma: Dimension-free robust stability of the Hayashi-Zhao common-label intersection from delta_B+delta_C and the I(A:B) cap, with a compatible local EB/recovery realization if that stronger conclusion is claimed.
